scope: G2 exploratory mechanism capability, actual local NATS native binary from fixed source. Not Runtime acceptance or cluster/power-loss proof.

cases.question: Publish acknowledgement and file-store process-crash persistence
cases.input: File stream, explicit sync_interval always, payload A under message-id r1, SIGKILL server after PubAck then restart same storage
cases.oracle: Independent new client reads original stream seq/payload/message-id; stream info confirms config. Do not claim OS/power failure from process crash.

cases.question: Deduplication identity versus content conflict
cases.input: Publish r1/A twice then r1/B within duplicate window
cases.oracle: Observe duplicate flags/sequence and stored original bytes. Native duplicate suppression must not be reported as content-conflict rejection if B returns ordinary duplicate acknowledgement.

cases.question: Historical input before wait registration
cases.input: Publish event before creating durable pull consumer with DeliverAll; close client and recreate
cases.oracle: Consumer receives exact pre-existing event, identity and payload from server, no producer replay.

cases.question: Unacknowledged redelivery across client loss
cases.input: Fetch message without ack, close client, after AckWait reopen durable consumer; ack-sync after refetch
cases.oracle: Same stream sequence redelivered, delivery count increases; acknowledgement floor advances, no pending ack after confirmed ack.

cases.question: Retention bounds do not disappear with durable consumer
cases.input: Separate stream max_msgs=1/discard old, publish A then B
cases.oracle: Fresh read of original seq reports absent, latest is B. This refutes assuming a durable consumer alone retains promised old content.

cases.question: Reject wrong mechanisms using same direct observers
cases.input: Separate memory stream killed with server; separate DeliverNew consumer created after prior event
cases.oracle: Old memory data unavailable after restart; DeliverNew receives no old message within bounded fetch. These are expected capability failures, not positive storage/history coverage.

execution: Local temp directory, localhost-only NATS, two clients; bounded waits <=3s for delivery, whole experiment <=90s; save all raw replies, server log/config, process exit and source/binary/dependency hashes. Exceptions and missing evidence FAIL, no silent skip. No secrets or external side effects.
